author: high
claim: The stated Sperner antichain theorem follows by permutation-chain double counting: every antichain \(\mathcal A\subseteq 2^{[n]}\) satisfies \(\sum_{A\in\mathcal A}\binom{n}{|A|}^{-1}\le 1\), hence \(|\mathcal A|\le \binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\), with equality attained by the \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor\)-level.
evidence: Let \(\mathfrak S_n\) be the set of all permutations \(\pi=(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_n)\) of \([n]\). For \(0\le j\le n\), put \(I_j(\pi)=\{\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_j\}\), with \(I_0(\pi)=\varnothing\). These sets form a strictly increasing chain, so at most one belongs to \(\mathcal A\). Count pairs \((A,\pi)\) such that \(A\in\mathcal A\) and \(A=I_{|A|}(\pi)\). Fixing \(\pi\) gives at most one pair, hence at most \(n!\) pairs total. Fixing \(A\) of size \(k\) gives exactly \(k!(n-k)!\) permutations, by independently ordering \(A\) in the first \(k\) positions and its complement afterward. Thus \(\sum_{A\in\mathcal A}|A|!(n-|A|)!\le n!\), equivalently \(\sum_{A\in\mathcal A}1/\binom n{|A|}\le1\). Put \(m=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\) and \(M=\binom nm\). For \(0\le k<m\), \(\binom n{k+1}/\binom nk=(n-k)/(k+1)\ge1\); symmetry \(\binom nk=\binom n{n-k}\) then gives \(\binom nk\le M\) for every \(0\le k\le n\). Therefore \(|\mathcal A|/M\le\sum_{A\in\mathcal A}1/\binom n{|A|}\le1\). Finally, all \(m\)-subsets form an antichain, because two distinct finite sets of equal size cannot contain one another, and their number is \(M\).

subgoals: derive the LYM inequality by double counting
prove the middle binomial coefficient is maximal

glossary.\\mathcal A: the given antichain family of subsets of [n]
glossary.\\mathfrak S_n: the set of all permutations of [n]
glossary.I_j(\\pi): the set of the first j entries of \pi
glossary.k: the cardinality of a fixed set A
